sermon.title: Jesus' Processing Plan, Part 1
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Jesus’ Processing Plan, Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Mark 3 to Mark 6 to show how Jesus called, made and sent his disciples: they followed him, responded to his call, spent time with him, were taught and shown his authority, and only then were sent to preach repentance, heal and cast out devils. He says everything starts with following Jesus and that authority comes only from Christ, not from titles or prophecies.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Several passages are quoted without naming the reference (e.g. Matthew 4:19, John 15:16, Matthew 26:40, Mark 6:4); the linked references are the passages he is quoting. At 21:00 he says Jesus raised a 12-year-old; the account is in Mark 5:41-42 (Jairus’s daughter), which he describes without naming. The figures he gives for crowds in Africa (“2 3 5,000 10,000 people”) are as spoken.

faqs.question: Can you go through Jesus’ processing plan at home?
faqs.answer: He says you cannot get it at home or in home Bible studies unless that home Bible study is the gathering together of the church; what God is doing he will do in his church.

faqs.question: Who decides who becomes an apostle, prophet, evangelist, pastor or teacher?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus Christ is still the deciding factor; he called unto him whom he would.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And He went up on the mountain and called to Him those He Himself wanted. And they came to Him.

faqs.question: Should you tell God you are not worthy to serve him?
faqs.answer: He says the disciples did not say “I’m not worthy” or point to their lives; they responded, “Jesus here I am, here I am, use me.”

faqs.question: Why is worship so important?
faqs.answer: He says worship should give us a chance to spend time with Jesus and take on his nature; many who want to get into the ministry do not know how to worship or pray.

faqs.question: What does he look for when he visits other ministries?
faqs.answer: He says he critiques to know whether people’s hearts are genuine or whether they have a hidden motive, such as wanting you to buy their books and follow their plan as the only plan.

faqs.question: Is it wrong to read the Bible through in a year?
faqs.answer: He says there is nothing wrong with that, but you need to take time to say “God open my understanding.”

faqs.question: What does he say about millions of years and evolution?
faqs.answer: He says when God said “let there be light” there was light, and when he spoke the plants and creatures came forth, with “no million year nonsense,” no evolution and no mutation.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.

faqs.question: Is grace and faith enough without repentance?
faqs.answer: He says grace and faith does not do anybody any good if they do not change their life, the way they talk, walk and treat people; he calls it icing on a spoiled cake.

faqs.question: Does God back up recovery programs or the message of repentance?
faqs.answer: He says God backed up the message of repentance, not the message of a 12 step program, and if repentance is not taught there will be no authority in the church.

faqs.question: Does God do miracles in every place?
faqs.answer: He says Paul did miracles in some cities and not others because God did not grant it; it is God’s business, schedule and purpose, and we just need to stick with him.

faqs.question: What happened when he preached in Africa?
faqs.answer: He says people would get healed while he was preaching and it had nothing to do with him; he challenged it, and found God came during the worship or the word and touched people, with salvations and healings.
